content.text:
Repository: /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin (OrcaSlicer fork "JusPrin"). Work in the worktree this session gives you; do not touch the main checkout. First run `git fetch origin` and move your worktree's branch to origin/jusprin-newui (20de313d92 or later; a rewritten history from 2026-10-14). Two other tasks are in flight on the same base and may touch AgentHost.cpp (one deletes the explain-only tool switch in handle_agent_tool_call; one renames ToolExecutionCoordinator::propose to submit). Keep your edits in that file small so they merge.

## What happened, in order

1. 2026-09-16, commits d5bf88a2e4 (project_open) and 24cec31df8 (printer_setup): the tools turned OrcaSlicer's two "unsaved changes" dialogs into refusals. project_open refuses when `Plater::is_project_dirty() || is_presets_dirty()` unless the model passes `unsavedWork: "discard"`; printer_setup refuses when the preset switch would drop unsaved preset edits unless `unsavedEdits: "discard"`. The refusal texts in src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/ToolExecutionCoordinator.cpp (near lines 681-683 and 716-719) say "Ask the user, then call again with discard" and "The open project has unsaved changes. Ask the user; save it first, or call again with unsavedWork discard". The adapter checks are in src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Workspace/OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp near lines 1021 and 2081, with the discard handling right after each.
2. 2026-09-29, commit 0412386910 (settings tools): the settings preview refuses to open a filament in its tab when another edited preset is dirty, issue code `unsaved_edits`, "Save or discard them in its settings first" (adapter near line 2623), and warns `saves_unsaved_edits` when a save would also save earlier unsaved edits (near 2633). The same commit added `check_filament_dialogs` in src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Workspace/OrcaSettings.hpp (lines 218-246), which, when a patch is saved with persistAs, pushes a blocking issue if the first-layer nozzle temperature is more than 30 °C from the other layers' (15 °C for a bed), mirroring the "continue?" question OrcaSlicer's Tab::save_preset asks through Tab::validate_filament_temperature_pairs (src/slic3r/GUI/Tab.cpp lines 6666 and 7238). That is a save-time validation question, not save-or-discard.
3. 2026-09-29, Kenneth's decisions (recorded in /Users/kenneth/.claude/projects/-Users-kenneth-Projects-JusPrin/memory/autosave-design-research.md): no save prompts; autosave like a well-behaved app; a way to go back, including undoing what the agent changed; settings edits are project-scoped by default and saved presets change only by an explicit act.
4. 2026-09-30, commit 076ed1d4c3 "Add managed project autosave and version history" (design: agent-docs/jusprin/autosave-version-history.md). Plater::close_with_confirm, new_project and load_project now call a `m_before_project_release` hook that saves the live state and proceeds instead of asking. Effective project settings are part of what a model version reconstructs, so a dropped preset edit is recoverable from version history. Agent mutations pin their before-state. This commit touched none of the tool paths in steps 1 and 2.
5. 2026-10-01, commit 832bb47c31 (file-opening report), developed in parallel and merged the same day: added `OrcaWorkspaceAdapter::file_open_can_replace_project` (adapter lines 518-524), called at the top of `Plater::load_project` (src/slic3r/GUI/Plater.cpp line 12144-12145 through `FileOpenScope::can_replace_project`), which stops opening another file with the message "The current project has unsaved changes. Opening another project was stopped; save or discard the current changes first." whenever Orca's `up_to_date()` tracker reports changes. It runs before the autosave hook gets a turn. The file-report prompt, src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/fileReportInstructions.ts, has a table row "Opening stopped because the current project has unsaved changes" telling the model to ask whether to save or discard.
6. 2026-10-07, commit eb45279cd5 removed tool-call approvals: every valid call starts at once. "Ask the user, then call again" is that removed design's vocabulary.
7. 2026-10-12, commit 2f308f2dda (now 0f46943de2 after the rewrite): the questions OrcaSlicer asks in Tab::on_value_change are forwarded by settings_preview_patch as warnings with code `orca_question` (rules in OrcaEditQuestions.hpp; design record in agent-docs/jusprin/mcp-tool-extension-guide.md under "Questions OrcaSlicer asks a person who edits a field"). The patch applies as sent and the agent settles the question: go ahead; go ahead and tell the user; or ask first when the answer is the user's. Kenneth chose this over refusing or holding for approval. The save-time question from step 2 was not part of it.

## What to do

Make every path follow the 2026-09-29 decision, and end with fewer lines than you started with; report the counts.

- project_open and printer_setup: remove the `unsavedWork` and `unsavedEdits` parameters, the refusals, and the "Ask the user" texts. Proceed the way the GUI now does: let the autosave hook save the live state (check what `m_before_project_release` does when `new_project` / `load_project` run from the tool path, and that it runs there), drop dirty preset edits silently as the discard branches already do, and say in the result what was dropped (the result already lists discarded edits). If a save fails the hook returns false and Orca cancels; surface that as the tool error, nothing else.
- The settings preview `unsaved_edits` refusal near adapter 2623: make it proceed on the same basis, or show with a test why it cannot. Keep the `saves_unsaved_edits` warning if it is informative; it is not a question.
- `file_open_can_replace_project` and the "Opening stopped" message: remove them, and remove the matching row from fileReportInstructions.ts and any test of that row. First confirm in the shell harness or by reading `Plater::up_to_date` whether the check still fires with autosave active; report what you found either way.
- The save-time temperature check in `check_filament_dialogs`: convert it from a blocking issue to an `orca_question` warning in the same shape as the edit-time ones (key, message in OrcaSlicer's words, suggestions when there are any, min and max when applicable), so the agent settles it the same way. Keep the volumetric-speed issue, which is a value OrcaSlicer resets, not a question. The workspace adapter harness in tests/workspace holds the edit-time rules to Tab.cpp; add the save-time case there.
- Update the tool descriptions in src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/ToolRegistry.cpp (project_open near line 1045, printer_setup near 1057) so they describe what happens, with no mention of asking; update the tool guide where it documents these parameters and codes (grep for unsavedWork, unsavedEdits, unsaved_work, unsaved_edits, "Opening stopped").
- Do not add any new confirmation, gate, or "the person agreed" field anywhere. Do not rewrite prompt sentences beyond deleting the table row; another task restructures the prompt.

## Verification

Build and run agent_bridge_tests and the workspace tests (recipe: /Users/kenneth/.claude/projects/-Users-kenneth-Projects-JusPrin/memory/jusprin-worktree-build.md; CMake from /Applications/CMake.app; reuse existing deps; BUILD_TESTS=ON; run long builds with nohup and a log, never as a background Bash command). Run the AgentUI vitest suite after the fileReportInstructions.ts change. Run the real-adapter harness in tests/workspace for the filament save case. Do not call any live model.

Commit on a branch in your worktree with a plain-English message that tells this story in a few lines and gives the line counts; do not push. Write a short untracked report in the worktree root (never commit it, never add it to .gitignore) for an engineer who did not see this session: what asked or refused before, what happens now, the autosave-check finding from step 5, and the net line count.

one selected in its collection). The tool works on the preset's edited
  copy, through its `Tab`, as for the process. Reads include the preset's
  unsaved edits.
- **Filament, when the target is another preset.** The preset must be in one
  of the project's slots; otherwise the call fails with `not_in_project`. It
  can be changed only by saving, so a call without `persistAs` fails with
  `not_selected`. Apply opens the preset in the filament tab the way the
  sidebar's edit button does: `Tab::select_preset`, then `set_filament_idx`
  for its slot. Apply then loads the change and saves it through the tab. If
  the filament that is open in the tab has unsaved edits, that switch would
  either discard them or show a prompt. So preview refuses with
  `unsaved_edits`.
- **Printer, when the target is another preset.** This is a saved printer
  that the project does not use. It can only be saved in place. The write
  goes through `Printers::write_unselected_printer`, which is the write
  `change_named_printer_nozzle` already makes: it stores the difference from
  the parent preset and queues the change for the cloud. Saving a copy of it
  would quietly create a second printer that the project does not know
  about. So a different `persistAs` fails with `not_selected`.
- A printer's blocked keys are the ones that decide which filament and
  process fit, or how many extruders there are (bed shape, nozzle size and
  type, extruder count, printer model), its network address and sign-in,
  and its identity as a preset. Those are 43 of its 160 settings. Custom
  g-code stays writable for a printer and a filament, as it was.
- Some settings hold one value per extruder or per nozzle kind. Such a
  setting keeps its length. A patch with a different number of values fails
  with `invalid_setting_value`, because a shorter list would drop the rest.

`persistAs` is not valid for `object`. For the preset scopes it works like
OrcaSlicer's Save with the name typed in:

- The preset's own name overwrites the preset. If OrcaSlicer ships that
  preset, the call fails with `read_only_preset`, and the suggestion is
  `"<name> - Copy"`, the name SavePresetDialog offers.
- Another name that no preset has saves a copy, and the copy takes the
  original's place. For a filament, that happens in every project slot that
  used the original (`Sidebar::update_presets_from_to`).
- A name that another preset has fails with `name_taken`.
- A name that SavePresetDialog would refuse fails with
  `invalid_preset_name`.

Saving the preset that is being edited also saves its other unsaved edits, as
Save does. Preview warns about this with `saves_unsaved_edits` and lists
those edits. The card's title says where the change is saved ("; save it", or
"; save as \"<name>\""). Without `persistAs`, the tool changes only the
edited preset and leaves it dirty.

In three cases the filament or printer tab would open a dialog. Preview
refuses these cases:

- a max volumetric speed below 0.5
  (`ConfigManipulation::check_filament_max_volumetric_speed`);
- a first-layer temperature that is further from the other layers'
  temperature than `Tab::validate_filament_temperature_pairs` allows when
  saving;
- firmware retraction with a wipe that retracts less than 100% first
  (`TabPrinter::toggle_options`).

### Scope expansion acceptance criteria

- The registry offers the same required `scope` enum and the same target
----
| a filament that is in none of the project's slots, changed by name | `not_in_project` |
| `persistAs` overwriting a preset Orca ships | `read_only_preset`, suggesting `"<name> - Copy"` |
| `persistAs` naming another existing preset | `name_taken` |
| `persistAs` SavePresetDialog would refuse | `invalid_preset_name` |
| key not in the definition table | `unknown_setting` with suggestions |
| known key not applicable to the requested scope | `unsupported_scope` |
| key on the write blacklist | `unsupported_setting_mutation` |
| read of a print host address or credential key | `withheld_setting`, per key under `unknownKeys`; the other keys are still read |
| requested object is gone, or no FFF printer or process is selected | `workspace_unavailable` |
| opening a filament in its tab would discard another dirty edited preset | `unsaved_edits` |
| parse failure, bound violation, or layer height outside the printer's range | `invalid_setting_value` with `allowed` or bounds |
| a scope-specific dependency or validator rule conflicts | `incompatible_settings` with the conflicting keys |
| session, revision, target mapping, preset, or before value changed since preview | `stale_workspace` with expected and current |
| client cancelled or the app closed | `cancelled` |
| the batch call failed after validation | `execution_failed` |

### Questions OrcaSlicer asks a person who edits a field

26:- **Dirty.** A preset is dirty when it has unsaved edits.
37:- **Connect** shows the person the command or the file edit and asks for confirmation first. name: live-test-built-app-on-mac
description: "How to launch, see, and drive the locally built JusPrin app on the Mac: the shared bundle id binds tools to the wrong instance, and \"on another Space\" usually means the window is on the second monitor, not that the user is in full screen."
metadata:

  originSessionId: fa2d66ed-e217-440b-aae0-da4164953edc
  modified: 2026-09-23T18:10:30.736Z

Every build of the fork (and /Applications/OrcaSlicer.app) shares bundle id `com.softfever3d.orca-slicer`. The desktop-control tools resolve an app by bundle id and bind to whichever instance comes first, so `app_list_windows` returns `[]` and filtered screenshots hide the window you actually launched.

**Working recipe (2026-09-05):** `ditto` the built .app into the scratchpad, `plutil -replace CFBundleIdentifier -string com.jusprin.worktree-test`, `codesign --force --deep -s -`, then `open -n <copy>.app --args <model>` and `request_access` for the new id. `app_screenshot`/`app_click` then work and include popup menus. A display-scope `left_click` on the header did NOT open the fork's PopupWindow menus, but a background `app_click` did; take the pixel-level `zoom` with the display tools afterwards (call `app_release` first). Display-scope `Escape` does not close those popups; a click elsewhere does.

The MCP discovery file `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/jusprin/mcp.json` points at the newest instance's `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp`; `tests/mcp/probe.py`'s `call()` can drive real tools (e.g. `workspace_inspect`, then `report_slice_review` with sessionId/plateId/sliceResultId) to put the header into the Check-print state without lldb. lldb `expr` cannot call inline accessors like `status_row()`.

**Why:** On 2026-09-01 a verification pass screenshotted the stock app instead of the build; on 2026-09-05 the tools bound to another session's main-repo build.

**How to apply:** Confirm the pid with `pgrep -fl OrcaSlicer.app/Contents/MacOS`; never kill an instance you did not launch. `osascript` System Events by unix id still works to set `frontmost`. See [[jusprin-shell-phase-1-design]] and [[orca-inherited-teardown-crash]].

**"On another Space" usually means "on the other monitor."** Cost about ten turns on
2026-09-09 and produced a wrong report to Kenneth. `app_list_windows` returns
`is_off_space: true` and clicks are refused with "this window is on another Space";
`app_bring_to_current_space` then fails with "the user's current Space is a full-screen
app." Both messages are about Spaces, so the natural read is that the user is sitting in
a full-screen app — but with *Displays have separate Spaces* on, a window merely sitting
on the second monitor produces exactly the same symptoms. Kenneth was not in full screen;
the harness had opened on the Acer.

Tell them apart before saying anything to the user: take a **display-scope** screenshot
(`app_release`, then `computer_batch` screenshot). Its header names the monitor it
captured and lists the others — if the window shows up there, it is a monitor problem,
not a Space problem, and the display-scope tools can drive it immediately. Never conclude
"the user is in a full-screen app" from the background tools' error text alone.

The same flag also flaps: a window can read `is_off_space: false` and click fine, then
read `true` a minute later. Clicks delivered while it is true report `ok ... unverified`
and silently do nothing. **A click that reports "unverified" and changes nothing is not
evidence of an application bug** — on 2026-09-09 that nearly became a filed defect about
being unable to retry after a failed MCP connect. Re-verify on a reachable window before

# No save prompts in agent tools: report

Commit a165018fc8 on branch `claude/no-save-prompts` (based on origin/jusprin-newui 20de313d92). Not pushed.

## Problem

On 2026-09-29 Kenneth decided JusPrin should never ask a person to save or discard: autosave keeps the work, and version history is the way back. Several paths built earlier still asked or refused:

- `project_open` refused when the project or a preset had unsaved changes, unless the agent passed `unsavedWork: "discard"` after asking the user. `printer_setup` did the same with `unsavedEdits` when a preset switch would drop edits.
- `settings_preview_patch` refused with `unsaved_edits` when saving a filament other than the one open in the filament tab, while the open one had edits.
- A filament save whose first-layer temperature was more than 30 °C from the other layers' (15 °C for a bed) was refused, because OrcaSlicer asks "Continue anyway?" before such a save.
- `Plater::load_project` called `file_open_can_replace_project`, which stopped any file open over unsaved changes with "Opening stopped…". This check ran before the autosave hook, and the agent prompt told the model to ask the user whether to save or discard.

## What happens now

- `project_open` always starts with Orca's `new_project`, which runs the autosave hook. The hook saves the open project, edited presets included. If that save fails, the tool returns "The open project could not be saved, so it stays open" and nothing else happens. After the save, edited presets are dropped and the file loads.
- `printer_setup` drops unsaved preset edits and lists them in `discarded`. The before-state is pinned, as it is for every agent change.
- Saving another filament drops the open filament's unsaved edits. Preview lists them in a `discards_unsaved_edits` warning. The `saves_unsaved_edits` warning stays.
- The temperature check is now an `orca_question` warning in OrcaSlicer's words, with the first-layer values Orca accepts as `min` and `max`. Apply answers Continue on Orca's dialog. The max-volumetric-speed refusal is unchanged.
- The "Opening stopped" check, its message and its prompt row are deleted. The tool descriptions and the tool guide now describe what happens, with no mention of asking.

**Finding on the old check:** it fired even with autosave running. Autosave writes with `SaveStrategy::Backup`, and that never resets the saved timestamp that `Plater::up_to_date(false, false)` reads. In the shell harness, after `autosave()->save_now()` succeeded on a changed project, `up_to_date` still returned false. So every open over a changed project was stopped, in the GUI too.

## Tests and results

All pass on a Release build:

- agent_bridge_tests: 276 cases
- workspace_contract_tests: 41 cases
- AgentUI vitest: 410 tests
- workspace adapter harness: 5,934 checks
- shell harness: 547 checks, 0 failures

New real-adapter cases:

- The forwarded save question matches the text of Orca's own dialog, which also shows a "Don't warn again" checkbox label after the question.
- The save goes ahead with no dialog.
- A save to another filament drops the open filament's edits, with no dialog.

The shell harness checks that a person's own open over a changed project, and the same open through the tool, both run without a dialog.

## Remaining issues

- `project_open` now calls `new_project` even when the project is clean. If a 3MF then fails to load, the project is left empty. This was already the case for a changed project, and `load_project` clears the old model in the same way.
- Two printer flows still refuse in save-or-discard words: printer connect and change in `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Printers/NamedPrinters.cpp` (around lines 363 and 406), and a nozzle change when the printer preset has unsaved edits. They were not part of this task.

**Line count:** 180 lines added, 183 removed (net −3). Without tests and docs: 86 added, 129 removed. `AgentHost.cpp` is untouched.

content.text:
The agent tools no longer ask the user to save or discard. Opening a project, switching presets and saving filament settings all go ahead now, and autosave and version history keep what would otherwise be lost. The commit is a165018fc8 on branch `claude/no-save-prompts`, based on origin/jusprin-newui 20de313d92, and is not pushed. It adds 180 lines and removes 183 (net −3). Leaving out tests and docs, it adds 86 and removes 129.

**What changed:**
- **`project_open`**: the `unsavedWork` parameter and its refusal are gone. The tool now starts with OrcaSlicer's `new_project`, which runs the autosave hook (`m_before_project_release`). The hook does run on this path. It saves the open project, including edited presets. If that save fails, the tool returns "The open project could not be saved, so it stays open" and nothing else happens. After the save, edited presets are dropped and the file loads.
- **`printer_setup`**: the `unsavedEdits` parameter and its refusal are gone. It drops unsaved preset edits and lists them in the result's `discarded` field, as before.
- **Settings preview, saving a filament other than the one open in its tab**: this used to be refused with `unsaved_edits`. It now goes ahead. The open filament's edits are dropped, and a `discards_unsaved_edits` warning lists them. The `saves_unsaved_edits` warning is kept.
- **Save-time temperature check**: it is now an `orca_question` warning in OrcaSlicer's words. Its `min` and `max` are the first-layer temperatures OrcaSlicer accepts. When the save runs, the tool answers OrcaSlicer's "Continue anyway?" dialog with Continue. The volumetric-speed refusal is unchanged.
- **"Opening stopped" check**: `file_open_can_replace_project`, its message and the matching row in `fileReportInstructions.ts` are deleted. No test covered that row.
- **Descriptions and guide**: the two tool descriptions in `ToolRegistry.cpp` and `mcp-tool-extension-guide.md` now describe what happens, with no mention of asking.
- `AgentHost.cpp` is untouched, so it should merge cleanly with the other two tasks.

**The "Opening stopped" check still fired with autosave running.** Autosave saves through `export_3mf` with `SaveStrategy::Backup`, which never resets the timestamp that `Plater::up_to_date(false, false)` reads. In the shell harness, I made a project dirty and ran `autosave()->save_now()`. The save succeeded, and `up_to_date` still returned false. So before this change, every open over a changed project was stopped, including a person's own File > Open in the GUI.

**Tests:** everything passes on a Release build in this worktree. No live model was called.

| Suite | Result |
|---|---|
| agent_bridge_tests | 276 test cases pass |
| workspace_contract_tests | 41 test cases pass |
| AgentUI vitest | 410 tests pass |
| Workspace adapter harness (real adapter) | 5,934 checks pass, exit 0 |
| Shell harness | 547 checks, 0 failures, exit 0 |

I added two cases to the workspace adapter harness:
- **Save-time question**: the forwarded text matches OrcaSlicer's own dialog word for word. The comparison allows for the "Don't warn again" checkbox label the dialog shows after the question. The save then completes with no dialog.
- **Saving another filament**: the open filament's edits are dropped, and nothing asks.

The shell harness now checks that a person's own open over a changed project, and the same open through `project_open`, both run with no dialog.

**Left as they were:**
- `project_open` now calls `new_project` even on a clean project. If a 3MF then fails to load, the project is left empty. That already happened when the project was dirty, and `load_project` clears the old model the same way.
- Two printer flows still refuse in save-or-discard words: printer connect and change in `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Printers/NamedPrinters.cpp` (around lines 363 and 406), and a nozzle change when the printer preset has unsaved edits. They weren't in this task's list.

The report for an engineer who didn't see this session is in the worktree root, untracked and not in `.gitignore`: [no-save-prompts-report.md](no-save-prompts-report.md).

The conclusion is that a definition adds cost to the *first* request of each conversation, not to every turn. That is why going over the budget only makes us look at the measurements and does not block a tool. Two things would change this conclusion: a catalog so large that the first request of every conversation is expensive by itself, or transcripts that show the model choosing the wrong tool. Watch for both. Neither has appeared yet.

**The printer panel follows the same rule with its own set of tools.** The printer panel on Home runs its own conversation, `PrinterConversation`. That conversation is offered the five printer tools and the four settings tools. The list is the same in every mode (Add, Change, or Connect), so it stays byte-identical through a conversation and between conversations of the same mode.

What a call may do depends on the conversation. `PrinterConversation::preflight_tool` refuses every call that is not allowed, before any card is shown, with an error that says where to go instead. The rules are:

- Finding and adding a printer (`printer_identify`, `printer_add`) is allowed only in an Add conversation. A Change or Connect conversation is about a printer the person already has. An add there would save another printer and move the conversation onto it.
- `printer_change` is allowed only on the printer the conversation is about, once there is one.
- The connection tools are allowed only once there is a saved printer.
- The settings tools are allowed only with `scope: "printer"`, on the printer the conversation is about.

A Change conversation may be about a stock profile (one that ships with OrcaSlicer) that the project has selected. That happens when the person chooses Printer settings… in the header on a project that uses a stock profile. In that case, changes to the nozzle and to the connection are refused with `stock_profile`. Changes to settings are saved as a copy of the profile, and the conversation follows that copy from then on (`PrinterConversation::tool_settled`). A Change conversation is never turned into an Add conversation. The code that opens a Change conversation checks that the printer is there, and shows OrcaSlicer's error dialog when it is not.

The header's filament chat uses the same panel (`PrinterPanel::open_filament`). It is offered the four settings tools and nothing else, and it gets no project state. It has its own instructions. The page writes them in `AgentUI/src/filamentInstructions.ts` and sends them with `filament_instructions`. The page writes them from the facts the app sends as the session part of the panel's state (`PrinterPanel::filament_session_json`): the preset's name, its slot and material, and, for a stock filament, the copy that a change is saved as. The preflight check for this chat allows the settings tools only with `scope: "filament"` on that preset. It refuses an apply that has no `persistAs`, with `not_saved`, because the chat is gone when it closes. When a copy is saved in the preset's place, the chat is about that copy from then on, and the page writes the instructions again for the copy. Until 2026-09-29 the filament chat ran on the project assistant's instructions and tools. With those, the model read "make the nozzle 5 degrees hotter" as a request to print. In another run it set 205 °C when the value was 220 °C, without reading the value first.

Yes, both parts are done. The project-open, printer-setup and settings changes from before are committed, and so are the printer changes you asked for. Everything is on branch `claude/no-save-prompts`, on top of the force-pushed jusprin-newui, and nothing is pushed. One thing is short of the original brief: the two commits together add 42 more lines than they remove.

**Printer changes (commit 7852470aff):**
- **Nozzle change:** it no longer refuses when the project's printer has unsaved edits. The saved profile is rewritten, the project's copy follows it, and `printer_change` lists the dropped settings in a new `discarded` field.
- **Your caveat about version history:** it was justified. The printer panel runs its own copy of the agent, and that copy had no "save a version first" step. A nozzle change from the panel would really have lost the dropped edits. The panel now saves a version first, the same way the main agent pane does before any change to the project. A test changes the nozzle through the panel, restores the version saved before it, and finds the dropped edit. I removed the new step and confirmed that the test fails without it.
- **Connect:** it no longer refuses. It only ever wrote the three connection settings, so the project's other unsaved edits stay, and nothing is dropped.
- **Rename:** it no longer opens Orca's save-or-discard prompt. I kept the edits instead of dropping them. Renaming saves the profile under its new name, and the unsaved edits are put back, still unsaved, on the same printer. Renaming a printer the project isn't using briefly selects it. If that switch dropped the project printer's edits, renaming some other printer would lose them, which would be surprising. If you'd rather have rename drop the edits, it's a small change.

**Tests:** I ran everything again on the final code, and it all passes:

| Suite | Result |
|---|---|
| Agent bridge unit tests | 273 cases pass |
| Workspace contract tests | 41 cases pass |
| Workspace adapter harness | 5,934 checks pass |

**Your reopen prompt: I think it's the right default, with two adjustments.**
1. **Ask the same way everywhere.** From reading the code, today the prompt appears only when a .3mf is dropped on the app or opened from Finder. File > Open Project (Cmd+O) skips it. I also believe a model file such as an STL never matches: the saved version seems to record the project's own file path, not the STL's, though I haven't confirmed that by running it. The agent's `project_open` doesn't check either.
2. **Notice when the file has changed since it was last opened.** The common case is someone re-exporting an STL from their CAD program to the same path. "Continue current project" would then quietly keep the old geometry. If the file's contents differ, the prompt should say so and make "Create new project" the default. If they match, "Open existing project" should be the default.

I agree that importing into a project should skip the check.

**Decisions for you:**
1. **The reopen prompt:** should I build it as above? That means one check shared by Cmd+O, drag-and-drop, Finder, Home and the agent, covering model files as well as .3mf, and noticing changed files. In the agent's case, the question would come back to the agent as a tool result, and the agent would ask you in chat instead of the app showing a window. Older projects may still contain `Auxiliaries/JusPrin/state.json` and a
recovery mirror. On first adoption, JusPrin reads that state and copies its
attachments to the managed store; it does not delete the old source. Once a
managed version exists, local state is authoritative. Reopening a copied
external 3MF with an already managed identity forks a new project identity.
When an external 3MF's source path matches a saved project, JusPrin asks
whether to create another project or open the existing one directly. If several
projects match, it continues the current one when it came from that file;
otherwise it opens the most recently updated match. The path
match is a reminder, not a content identity check: a changed file at the same
path still offers the choice.
Earlier local versions with `state.json` and a model-bound document sidecar
remain readable; the first new document write upgrades them to the independent
current-document format without rewriting historical versions.
Recent projects appear on Home and in the header menu. Selecting one
opens its managed version even when its imported source file has been removed.

description: "How to capture the fork's wx popup menus on macOS for a pixel comparison against Windows captures, and why Windows text renders ~9% larger than the tokens intend."
metadata:

---

To compare Windows screenshots against macOS, run the same
`shell_integration_harness` fixture on both and capture each popup by window id.

**Why:** `screencapture` and any ScreenCaptureKit path fail from the Bash tool
("could not create image from display") — the Screen Recording grant belongs to a
process I cannot reach. The computer-use `app_screenshot` tool is the only route,
and it accepts a **raw CGWindowID**, not just ids from `app_list_windows`. Popups
never appear in `app_list_windows`, so enumerate them yourself.

**How to apply:**
- Build a tiny Swift lister (`CGWindowListCopyWindowInfo(.optionOnScreenOnly)`
  filtered by pid). The fork's `HeaderMenu` popups show up at `layer=101`; the main
  window is `layer=0`. Feed that id to `app_screenshot` for native-resolution pixels.
- Drive clicks with a Swift `CGEvent` helper at **global** coords
  (window origin + local). The app need not be frontmost.
- Only the **chip halves** respond to synthetic clicks. The header's overflow "…",
  the split-button chevron, and the Home back button do not — that is a limitation
  of the automation, **not** an application bug. Use the harness's own
  `--header-visual` / `--review-visual` modes for those screens instead.
- While a popup is open, the next click anywhere only dismisses it. Budget two
  clicks. Escape does not close them.
- Put the window on the **Acer H226HQL** (1920x1080, non-Retina): the harness's
  1200x800 window is then 1:1 with a Windows capture at 100% scaling, so popup
  sizes compare directly. On the built-in Retina display they would not.

**Windows text is ~9% LARGER than macOS, not smaller.** `Label::sysFont`
(`src/slic3r/GUI/Widgets/Label.cpp:19`) multiplies the point size by 4/5 off Apple
to offset Windows' 96 DPI against macOS' 72 — but 96/72 x 4/5 = 1.067, so it
under-corrects. Measured on the chip: glyph height 12 px Windows vs 11 px macOS.
Consequence: fixed-width popups ellipsize *more* on Windows. Do not assume the 4/5
factor makes Windows text smaller. Mono text goes the other way (Courier New is
narrower than Menlo), so the chip itself comes out 346 px on Windows vs 353 on Mac.

See [[live-test-built-app-on-mac]], [[windows-gui-test-vm-gcp]],
[[render-widget-to-bitmap-for-visual-proof]].

On 2026-09-23 a full live walkthrough of the printer panel was driven with display-scope `computer_batch` (`zoom` + `save_to_disk: true`). Every call returned the image, but no path was reported and a disk-wide search found no file. Do not count on `save_to_disk` for deliverables.

**What worked for files:** the [[fake-host-page-fixture]] recipe under the Playwright MCP. Copy `resources/jusprin/agent/index.html` (and `home/index.html`), inject `window.wx` + a `window.SCENES` table of full `state` payloads, serve with `python3 -m http.server`, open `agent.html?panel=printer`, switch scenes with `browser_evaluate` and save with `browser_take_screenshot` (`scale: device`, `filename` under the repo's `.playwright-mcp/`, the only allowed root; move the PNGs out and `rm -rf .playwright-mcp` afterwards so `git status` stays clean). Real printer pictures come from `resources/profiles/<Vendor>/<Model>_cover.png` as data URLs. The credential card renders from a `toolActivities` entry with `tool: 'printer_connect'`, `correlationId` = an assistant message id, state `pending` (card) or `succeeded` ("Sent"). Chips come from a trailing `Choices: a | b` line. 13 scenes took about 10 minutes and matched the live rendering.

**Window overlap trap:** when another session runs `JusPrinShellHarness --printer-live` in a loop, each run opens a 1200x800 window at the same origin (360,125) on the primary display and takes the front, so display-scope zooms and clicks land on *its* window. Move your own instance by pid with a 20-line Swift AX helper (`AXUIElementCreateApplication(pid)` → `kAXPositionAttribute`) onto the built-in display (bounds start at y=1080 here), then `switch_display "Built-in Retina Display"`. The first display click only focuses the window; click again. `--manual-live-agent` does not enable the fake Bambu printer, so the Bambu connect path is out of reach in manual mode.

**Why:** the walkthrough's evidence would otherwise have been lost, and a click into the other session's scripted run could have corrupted its result.

**How to apply:** for any "take screenshots" request on the web pages, plan on the fixture route for files from the start and use the live app only to observe. See [[live-test-built-app-on-mac]] and [[printer-live-harness-lessons]].

Both parts are done and committed on `claude/no-save-prompts`, not pushed. The nozzle change can no longer drop unsaved edits that exist nowhere else. The "previously opened file" question now appears however the file is opened, and notices when the file has changed.

**Nozzle change (commit d33fb306c9).** You were right that my earlier version could drop edits without keeping them. Only the printer panel's agent saved a version first; the nozzle-change function itself didn't. The function now refuses to switch until the unsaved edits are saved to the project's version history:
- If saving fails, or the caller has no way to save, the nozzle stays as it was and the person is told why.
- The printer panel saves through autosave.
- Tests cover all three cases: no way to save, saving fails, and saving succeeds. In the last, restoring the saved version brings the edits back.

**Reopen question (commit 849b2b516a).** The four screenshots are attached and also in `reopen-prompt-screenshots/` in the worktree. The app drew them itself; I didn't use screen access, since you declined it. On a Mac the default choice is the first, blue button. The generic icon is only because the test app has none.
- **Every way of opening asks:** File > Open Project, recent files, Finder and dragging a file onto the app. Before, only Finder and drag-and-drop asked.
- **Changed files:** each project now remembers which file it came from and a fingerprint of that file's contents. If the file has changed since, the question says so and defaults to "Create new project". Otherwise it defaults to the existing project.
- **The agent:** it no longer opens the file straight away. It gets back the project's name and whether the file changed, along with this instruction: "Ask the person whether to continue that project or start a new one from the file." It then calls again with your answer. This now covers model files (STL and the like) too, which were never matched before.
- **Importing:** adding a file into a project still never asks.

The agent tests (273 cases), the workspace tests (41 cases, plus 5,934 checks in the full-app workspace test) and the AgentUI web tests (410) all pass. So do the end-to-end tests in the default (547 checks), printer (199) and reopen (77) modes.

**One thing to confirm.** Your original brief said not to add any new confirmation step to the agent tools. The reopen question does add one: `project_open` now waits for "existing" or "new" when a file was opened before. I did that on purpose because you asked for the question. Tell me if you'd rather the agent pick a default and just say what it did.

Separately, I found a rare crash risk in existing code. If the agent sends a tool call that fails immediately, right after a new project is created and before that project has been saved even once, the app reads a record that was just deleted. Normal use waits between steps, so I haven't seen it outside my test, and I didn't fix it. It's written up in the untracked report, [no-save-prompts-report.md](no-save-prompts-report.md).

It gets back the project’s name and whether the file changed, along with this instruction: “Ask the person whether to continue that project or start a new one from the file.” It then calls again with your answer. First, I am pretty sure a old version of the dialogue already existed. Be sure you reuse the old one rather than the duplicating a similar function. Second, the screenshot you show were really ugly. I think other agents have made a similar mistake when they were using system native dialogues rather than the shared dialog the upstream orcaslicer already had. Check to see if you have made the same mistake, if so, fix it in a similar way and add to This as a lesson to the Knowledge Sharing Engineering doc under agent-docs

> Nozzle change (commit d33fb306c9). You were right that my earlier version could drop edits without keeping them. Only the printer panel’s agent saved a version first; the nozzle-change function itself didn’t. The function now refuses to switch until the unsaved edits are saved to the project’s version history:
> 
> If saving fails, or the caller has no way to save, the nozzle stays as it was and the person is told why.
> The printer panel saves through autosave.
> Tests cover all three cases: no way to save, saving fails, and saving succeeds. In the last, restoring the saved version brings the edits back.

When this refusal goes back to the agent, will the agent process in the same way as other orca questions?

No, and it shouldn’t be. They’re two different kinds of result.

An OrcaSlicer question is a warning with code orca_question, returned by settings_preview_patch. It means: this change is valid and will apply as sent, but a person making it by hand would see this question. The agent settles it before applying the patch. It can go ahead, go ahead and tell the user, or ask the user first when the answer is theirs. The guidance for this lives in the settings_preview_patch tool description in ToolRegistry.cpp, not in any prompt.

This refusal is a plain tool error, code change_failed, returned by printer_change. Nothing happened: the nozzle wasn’t changed because the unsaved printer edits couldn’t be saved to version history first. There’s no question to settle and no “go ahead” option. The model handles it like any other failed tool call. It reads the message and decides what to say, and the failed tool card already shows the person the sentence.

Two things follow from that:

There’s no specific guidance for this failure. The printer prompt (printerInstructions.ts) gives instructions after a failed connection (lines 156-157) and for settings the tools refuse (line 59). It says nothing about change_failed from printer_change, and it doesn’t mention orca_question at all. So the agent improvises here, and I haven’t measured what it does.
Making it an OrcaSlicer question would be wrong. That would mean the change applies anyway and the agent decides whether to mention it. The whole point of this refusal is that the nozzle must not change while the edits exist nowhere else. A failed save to version history is a fault to report, not a choice for the user. The useful next step is to try again. Failing that, the person can save or discard the printer edits in Printer settings, then change the nozzle.
If you want the agent to say something consistent here, the fix is one line in the printer prompt about change_failed. That would mean editing prompt text, which the original brief said another task owns, so it’s your call.

So this behavior is wrong too. But let's keep it here. Creates a test chip to look into what's the right way to handle it.


one last thing: orca_questions is a bad name. Rename it to something that would reflect its nature better. If you do not understand why this function was created, go back to git log and In session history to find out. Make sure you give it a relevant name for its purpose and scope. Make sure you change both the code and the document so that it's easier for us to discuss this and for you to think things through when we are making changes related to this function again.

Four things to do: check that I reused the old reopen dialog, switch it to OrcaSlicer's shared dialog and record the lesson, file a task chip for how the agent handles the nozzle failure, and rename `orca_question`. Starting with the doc and history research.

# JusPrin engineering and verification method

**Status:** Required planning, implementation, and release-verification method for `jusprin-newui`.

JusPrin is changing the presentation of a mature manufacturing application. The main engineering risk is not whether common UI technology can work; it is whether new presentation code bypasses, duplicates, or destabilizes authoritative Orca behavior.

## Risk vocabulary

Risk means residual, evidence-backed uncertainty that could materially affect architecture, correctness, delivery, regressions, or a physical print after mature precedent has been considered.

Keep these categories separate:

- **Feasibility:** whether a technical boundary can work at all.
- **Integration:** whether proven components can be connected without unsafe ownership or duplicated behavior.
- **Product behavior:** uncertainty about what the feature must do.
- **Delivery effort:** understood implementation work, even when substantial.
- **Regression exposure:** risk of disturbing mature Orca behavior.
- **Platform QA:** evidence required for a particular OS, WebView backend, display stack, input method, or DPI.

A known bug, untested platform, or inconvenient implementation detail is not automatically an architecture risk.

## Required assessment process

Before adding a spike or assigning a risk label:

1. Define the user-visible requirement without assuming an implementation or cause.
2. Classify the underlying technical capability.
3. Search for mature precedent in the current Orca code, Orca history and forks, comparable slicers, mature same-stack applications, and finally framework documentation.
4. State what the precedent proves and where it differs.
5. Isolate only the unproven delta.
6. Record the plausible failure, evidence for likelihood, consequence, blast radius, reversibility, and cheapest resolving evidence.
7. Choose code inspection, a focused test, an integration prototype, platform validation, or a feasibility spike according to the uncertainty.

A new visual arrangement is not necessarily a new technical capability. Spike only consequential uncertainty that mature code and focused tests cannot answer.

## Current evidence ledger

| Requirement | Established evidence | Remaining production delta | Current classification |
|---|---|---|---|
| Native shell | Orca already composes native panels and `GLCanvas3D`; the exact native/WebView boundary ran on macOS and Linux/X11 | Production shell behavior and remaining platform/input coverage | Very low feasibility; integration and platform QA remain |

Hand OrcaSlicer's edit-time questions to the agent as preview warnings

When a person changes certain settings in OrcaSlicer's settings panel,
OrcaSlicer asks a question first: "smooth timelapse needs a prime tower,
enable it?", "this will change the shape of your model, are you sure?",
"change the recommended support settings for you?". The code that asks is
Tab::on_value_change, which runs for one field at a time. The settings tools
apply a patch through Tab::load_config, which never runs it. Since the tools
were allowed to change every setting except a short blacklist (5dadfe2801),
a patch could change these settings and nobody was asked or told.

settings_preview_patch now returns one warning per question, with code
orca_question:

- key: the setting the question is about;
- message: the question as a person would read it, whole;
- suggestions: the values OrcaSlicer's Yes would set, as key=value,
  leaving out any that already hold;
- min and max, for layer height: the nozzles' limits.

The patch stays valid and applies as sent. The agent settles the question
one of three ways, which the tool description spells out: go ahead; go
ahead and tell the user; or ask the user first, when the answer is theirs
to give. Kenneth chose this on 2026-10-12 over refusing the change, holding
it for approval, or blacklisting the settings. A valid tool call already
starts at once, and a "the person agreed" field would only be the agent's
word.

The rules are forward_edit_questions in the new OrcaEditQuestions.hpp, a
copy of the conditions in Tab.cpp for the process, object, filament and
printer scopes: the prime tower with smooth timelapse, clumping detection
or precise Z height; print by object on a bed-slinger; the support
filaments; make_overhang_printable; sparse_infill_rotate_template; layer
height outside the nozzles' limits; the two long retraction switches. No
OrcaSlicer file changes. A question is raised only for a setting the patch
really changes, with its condition read from the values the patch leaves,
so a patch that sends the companion value with the change raises nothing,
and neither does a state a person chose earlier.

give every queued callback an explicit lifetime token; closing a window does not
make captured objects safe.

### A parented top-level shell did not have an independent lifetime

**Observed problem:** The first opaque shell was a top-level `wxFrame` parented
to the legacy OrcaSlicer frame. On macOS, destroying the probe also caused the
tracked legacy frame and shell to be destroyed. A parent relationship chosen for
window stacking had unintentionally coupled the windows' lifetimes.

**Resolution:** The shell became an unparented top-level window. It explicitly
observes legacy move, size, visibility, activation, and destruction events, while
the probe remains owned by the shell. The final run destroyed the probe while
the application, legacy frame, and opaque shell remained alive.

**Lesson for future agents:** Treat wx top-level parenting as lifecycle
ownership, not as a harmless z-order hint. Windows that must survive
independently should have independent ownership and explicit lifecycle
observation.

### Native choice dismissal moved focus to the opaque shell

**Observed problem:** Dismissing the native macOS `wxChoice` popup could leave
the opaque shell as the key window. The probe still existed, but it was no longer
the usable window above the shell.

**Resolution:** The choice handler schedules probe `Raise()` and control
`SetFocus()` calls with `CallAfter`, after the native popup has completed its own
focus transition.

**Lesson for future agents:** Focus after a native popup is asynchronous. Check

### Questions OrcaSlicer asks a person who edits a field

`Tab::on_value_change` in `Tab.cpp` runs when a person changes one field. For
some settings it shows a question first. `Tab::load_config` never runs it, so
a patch changes those settings and nobody is asked. The question goes to the
caller instead.

Kenneth decided this on 2026-10-12. The caller is an agent, and it settles
the question itself, one of three ways: go ahead; go ahead and tell the user;
or ask the user first, when the answer is theirs to give (it depends on what
the object is for, or it accepts a risk to their printer). No tool refuses
these changes, holds them for approval, or records that a person agreed. The
description of `settings_preview_patch` tells the caller this.

Preview adds one warning per question, with code `orca_question`:

- `key` is the setting the question is about.
- `message` is the question as the person would read it, whole. It comes
  from the translation catalog, so it is in the interface language.
- `suggestions` are the values OrcaSlicer's Yes would set, as `key=value`,
  leaving out any that already hold. A caller accepts by adding them to the
  patch.
- `min` and `max`, for layer height, are the nozzles' limits; for a
  first-layer temperature, the values OrcaSlicer saves without asking.

`Tab::save_preset` also asks, per `Tab::validate_filament_temperature_pairs`;
with `persistAs`, preview forwards that as above (`forward_save_questions`).

The warning leaves the patch valid, and the patch applies as sent. The apply
result does not repeat it.

The rules are `forward_edit_questions` in `OrcaEditQuestions.hpp`. They are a
copy of the conditions in `Tab.cpp`, and they look each message up in the
catalog piece by piece, as `Tab.cpp` does. Three things follow from how
OrcaSlicer asks:

- A question is about a setting the patch really changes. A value the
  normalizer puts straight back (clumping detection on a printer without it)
  raises nothing.
- The condition is read from the values the patch leaves. A patch that sends
  the companion value with the change (smooth timelapse together with the
  prime tower) raises nothing.
- A state a person chose earlier by answering "do it anyway" raises nothing
  on a later patch that leaves those settings alone.

An object override raises the same questions as the process setting, because
OrcaSlicer's object panel runs the same handler.

| Setting | OrcaSlicer asks when the change leaves | Yes sets |
|---|---|---|
| `enable_prime_tower` off | smooth `timelapse_type`; and then a second question if `enable_wrapping_detection` is on. Clumping detection alone raises nothing | nothing (No turns the tower back on) |
| `enable_prime_tower` on | `precise_z_height` on | nothing |
| `enable_wrapping_detection` on | the prime tower off | nothing |
| `precise_z_height` on | the prime tower on | nothing |
| `timelapse_type` smooth | the prime tower off | `enable_prime_tower=1` |
| `print_sequence` by object | a printer whose `printer_structure` is `i3` | nothing |
| `support_filament` | a filament OrcaSlicer counts as support material (`is_support_filament`, not strict) that is not soluble, in a project where no object uses TPU | nothing (No sets it back to 0) |
| `support_interface_filament` | a support material without all of top Z distance 0, interface spacing 0 and the interlaced rectilinear pattern; or a soluble interface over a base that is not | those three values, `independent_support_layer_height=0`, and sometimes `support_filament` |
| `make_overhang_printable` on | always | nothing |
| `sparse_infill_rotate_template` given where there was none | a pattern other than rectilinear, line, zigzag, cross zag or locked zag | nothing |
| `layer_height` | a height below the lowest `min_layer_height` or above the highest `max_layer_height` of the printer's nozzles | the nearer limit |
| `long_retractions_when_cut` (printer) or `filament_long_retractions_when_cut` (filament) on for an extruder | always. This one has only an OK button: OrcaSlicer informs, it does not ask | nothing |

The copy is held to the original by the workspace adapter harness. It makes
each change the way a field does (the value into the tab's config, then
OrcaSlicer's own `on_value_change`), with every dialog the handler opens
answered and written down, and compares those dialogs with the questions
preview forwarded. `verify_edit_questions` does this for a case per row and
for the cases that must raise nothing. `verify_every_writable_setting` does
it for every setting it applies, so a question upstream adds, drops or
rewords fails the sweep with `Orca asks ..., preview forwarded ...` and the
setting's name. After an upstream update, run the harness and bring the
rules and this table back in line with `Tab.cpp`.

input.title: Decide how the agent handles a refused nozzle change
input.tldr: Today a nozzle change refuses when the printer's unsaved edits can't be saved to version history, and the agent gets a bare tool error with no guidance. Kenneth says that behavior is wrong too. This task works out the right handling and proposes it.
input.prompt:
Repository: /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin (OrcaSlicer fork "JusPrin"). Work in your own git worktree, based on the branch `claude/no-save-prompts` (local, unpushed, in worktree .claude/worktrees/hungry-bartik-ceb424; commits d33fb306c9 and 7852470aff are the relevant ones) or on origin/jusprin-newui once that branch is merged. Do not touch the main checkout or another session's worktree.

Background. On 2026-09-29 Kenneth decided JusPrin never asks a person to save or discard: autosave keeps the work and version history is the way back. On 2026-10-14 the printer nozzle change was changed to follow that rule: `change_named_printer_nozzle` in src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Printers/NamedPrinters.cpp drops the project printer's unsaved edits only after a caller-supplied step (`keep_unsaved_edits`, which pins an autosave version; supplied by ShellController through PrinterPanel::Callbacks) has saved them to version history. If that step is missing or fails, the nozzle is not changed and the function returns the message "The unsaved changes to this printer couldn't be saved to the project's history, so the nozzle was not changed." The printer panel's `printer_change` tool (PrinterConversation::change in src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/PrinterSetup/PrinterConversation.cpp) turns that into a plain tool error with code `change_failed`.

The open question. Kenneth said this behavior is wrong too, without saying what is right. Today the agent improvises: the printer prompt (src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/printerInstructions.ts) has guidance after a failed connection and for refused settings, but nothing about `change_failed` from `printer_change`. It is NOT an OrcaSlicer confirmation (warning code `skipped_confirmation`, returned by settings_preview_patch for a valid patch that applies as sent), and must not become one: the nozzle must never change while the edits exist nowhere else.

What to do: investigate and propose the right handling, for example whether the failure should be retried automatically, carry a distinct error code and recovery steps in the result, change how the panel presents it, or get one sentence of prompt guidance (prompt text is restructured by another task, so coordinate before editing printerInstructions.ts). Read agent-docs/jusprin/mcp-tool-extension-guide.md (printer panel section) and agent-docs/jusprin/autosave-version-history.md first. Reproduce the failure path with the shell harness (`JusPrinShellHarness --printer-setup`; checks named nozzle_change_whose_keeper_fails_leaves_unsaved_edits and nozzle_panel_*). Do not call any live model without Kenneth approving a specific batch. Write your proposal for Kenneth in plain English: what happens today, the options with consequences, your recommendation. Do not push.

content.text:
All four items are done and committed on `claude/no-save-prompts` (not pushed), and every test suite passes. One of my commits doesn't build on its own; fixing that needs your OK, covered at the end.

**1. Reusing the old dialog.** I didn't duplicate it. "Previously opened file" was always the existing handler in `ShellController`, and I extended that handler rather than copying it. The agent's path shows no dialog at all; it reuses the same lookup of earlier projects.

**2. The ugly dialog (commit d7c62b4534).** Yes, I made the same mistake. The old dialog, and my change to it, used `wxMessageDialog`, which on a Mac is a system alert. The earlier fix by another agent is `offer_agent_setup` in `ShellController`, which switched to OrcaSlicer's own `MessageDialog`. I did the same:
- **Button order:** OrcaSlicer's dialog always highlights its Yes button, so I put the suggested choice there. That's "Create new project" when the file changed, and the existing project otherwise.
- **Getting the dialog to the person:** while a person opens a file, the app automatically answers every OrcaSlicer dialog. Switching dialogs alone would have meant this question was cancelled before anyone saw it. A dialog listener can now let one specific dialog through to the person, and this question uses that for itself only.
- **Screenshots:** the new ones are attached.
- **The lesson:** no document is named "Knowledge Sharing Engineering". The one that collects lessons for future agents is `agent-docs/jusprin/orca-integration-guide.md`, so I added it there. Tell me if you meant a different document.
- **Elsewhere:** other JusPrin code still uses system alerts, mostly error messages in the left pane and status row. I left those alone.

**3. The nozzle-change refusal.** It's unchanged, and a task chip is filed: "Decide how the agent handles a refused nozzle change." The chip states the constraint: the nozzle must never change while the unsaved edits exist nowhere else, so this must not become a skipped confirmation.

**4. The rename (commit dfd89a1379).** `orca_question` is now `skipped_confirmation`. I based the name on the commit that created it: the warning marks a confirmation OrcaSlicer would ask of a person making that change, or saving it, by hand. The patch skips that confirmation and applies as sent, and the agent settles it. It's not a refusal. The rename covers the code, the rule file (now `SkippedConfirmations.hpp`), the test names, the tool description and the tool guide. The guide section is now titled "Skipped confirmations" and notes the old name.

**Tests:** I ran everything again after these changes, and it all passes:

| Suite | Result |
|---|---|
| Agent unit tests | 273 test cases |
| Workspace tests | 41 test cases |
| Full-app workspace test | 5,934 checks |
| End-to-end, default mode | 547 checks |
| End-to-end, printer mode | 199 checks |
| End-to-end, reopen mode | 77 checks |
| Dialog capture | passes |

**One thing needs your OK.** The renamed file was already staged when I made the dialog commit, so the rename landed in d7c62b4534 instead of dfd89a1379. As a result d7c62b4534 doesn't build on its own; the branch tip does. Fixing it means rewriting those two unpushed commits so the rename moves into the second one. Should I do that?

git status --short | grep -v "^??"; git branch backup/no-save-prompts-before-squash HEAD; git reset --soft 7b2441dfd4 && git diff --cached --shortstat && git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
No save-or-discard prompts; ask only about files opened before

On 2026-09-29 Kenneth decided JusPrin never asks a person to save or
discard: autosave keeps the work and version history is the way back.
Several paths still refused or asked. This brings them in line, and makes
the one question that remains, about a file opened before, consistent.

Save or discard:
- project_open releases the project through new_project, whose autosave
  hook saves it first; a failed save is the tool error. unsavedWork and the
  refusal are gone. Edited presets are dropped after the save.
- printer_setup drops unsaved preset edits and lists them in discarded;
  unsavedEdits and its refusal are gone.
- Saving another filament drops the open filament's unsaved edits and
  warns discards_unsaved_edits instead of refusing.
- Plater::load_project no longer stops opening a file over unsaved changes.
  That check fired even with autosave running, because autosave never
  resets Orca's own save tracker. Its prompt-table row is gone.
- A printer's nozzle change on the project's printer changes only after
  the unsaved edits are saved to version history; otherwise nothing
  changes. The printer panel's agent saves a version before printer_change,
  which lists the dropped keys in discarded.
- Connecting a printer keeps the project's other unsaved edits; renaming a
  printer no longer raises Orca's prompt and keeps the edits unsaved.

Skipped confirmations:
- orca_question is renamed skipped_confirmation (SkippedConfirmations.hpp):
  a confirmation OrcaSlicer asks of a person who makes a change, or saves
  it, by hand, which a patch skips. The save-time first-layer temperature
  check is now one of them instead of a refusal.

Files opened before:
- The "Previously opened file" question runs in Plater::load_project, so
  every way a person opens a .3mf asks. Each version records the file the
  project came from and its MD5; a changed file defaults to a new project.
  The agent's project_open returns opened_before and takes openedBefore.
- The question uses OrcaSlicer's MessageDialog, not a system alert. A
  dialog listener may return kShowToPerson to let one dialog through to
  the person while a file open answers the rest. Recorded as a lesson in
  the OrcaSlicer integration guide.

Harness checks cover each path; --reopen-prompt draws the dialog to PNGs.
EOF

# No save prompts in agent tools: report

All of this landed on jusprin-newui as one commit, 336facf825 ("No save-or-discard prompts; ask only about files opened before"), on top of 6b4b8b6188. It changes 41 files, adding 836 lines and removing 368. The commit hashes in the sections below are from before the squash.

content.text:
All my changes are now a single commit, 336facf825, pushed to jusprin-newui as a fast-forward on top of the force-pushed branch. It changes 41 files, adding 836 lines and removing 368, and every test suite passes on that exact commit.

**Rebasing onto the new base:** the force-pushed branch added two commits, one sweeping approval wording out of prompts and docs and one moving the assistant's prompt into the Agent page. My commit conflicted with the wording sweep in three places, all in sentences my commit deletes (the old "discard" instructions for `project_open` and `printer_setup`). The sweep had changed nothing else there, so I kept my side. The moved prompt mentions none of the removed parameters.

**An intermittent failure I fixed before landing:** the first test run on the rebased build failed two reopen checks once.
- **Cause:** autosave could start tracking a freshly opened .3mf before OrcaSlicer had set the project's file name. The project then never recorded which file it came from, so a reopen couldn't tell whether the file had changed.
- **Fix:** when a project's first version is saved, autosave now records the project file if nothing is recorded yet.
- **Evidence:** before the fix, the missing record showed up in about one run in ten. After it, six runs in a row passed.

**Final results on 336facf825:**

| Suite | Result |
|---|---|
| Agent unit tests | 277 cases pass |
| Workspace tests | 41 cases pass |
| Agent page tests | 413 pass |
| Full-app workspace test | 5,934 checks pass |
| End-to-end, default mode | 550 checks pass |
| End-to-end, printer mode | 199 checks pass |
| End-to-end, reopen mode | 77 checks pass |
| Dialog capture | passes |

**Left behind:**
- The local branch `backup/no-save-prompts-before-squash` holds the six commits before the squash. I can delete it if you don't need it.
- I didn't touch the main checkout, so its local `jusprin-newui` branch hasn't been updated.
- The untracked report is updated and stays out of the commit: [no-save-prompts-report.md](no-save-prompts-report.md).
